topic: on-device doc-QA model comparison (FoundationModels vs Gemma vs Qwen)
question: Which on-device model is best for CUAD document Q&A — Apple FoundationModels, Gemma 4 E2B, or Qwen2.5-1.5B?
lesson: Gemma 4 E2B beat FoundationModels on balanced accuracy by 14.5 pts (CI +11.3..+17.6), mainly by abstaining on unanswerable items (65% vs 39%). FM is weak at saying 'absent'. Baseline key-fact ~67.9%.

question: What recall does hybrid (0.7 semantic + 0.3 BM25) retrieval achieve on CUAD?
lesson: Established the 61.4% recall@3 baseline with EmbeddingGemma (35.2% with NLEmbedding). Embedding quality matters: a 26-point gap between embedders. This is the number every retrieval idea is measured against.

question: Which embedding model is best for on-device CUAD retrieval, and does an absence instruction help doc QA?
lesson: EmbeddingGemma beat the alternatives tested. A plain 'if not in the sections, say so' instruction improved contract QA faithfulness. Prefer EmbeddingGemma unless a new idea beats it on a measured recall basis.

question: How many chunks (top-K) should be retrieved for Qwen doc QA?
lesson: K=3 chunks is optimal; more chunks added distractors and hurt answer quality. Ideas that increase retrieved context should justify why they beat K=3.

question: Can BM25-only match hybrid recall while removing the 600MB embedding model?
lesson: BM25-only recall was ~15 points below hybrid on CUAD; semantic embeddings are necessary. Do NOT re-propose dropping semantic retrieval for pure lexical — it's settled.

question: Does prepending document/section context to chunks before embedding improve recall, like Anthropic's contextual embeddings?
lesson: Failed because the implementation (naive static title/heading prepend) did NOT match Anthropic's method (model-GENERATED per-chunk context + contextual BM25 + reranking). Lesson: verify the actual mechanism of a cited result before adopting it; a naive imitation is not the method.

question: Does a lightweight cross-encoder reranker over hybrid candidates improve recall@3 / is it worth the device cost?
lesson: Parked for device, then its host stage was executed in PoC-027 and REJECTED (off-the-shelf rerankers degrade hard categories). Do not re-propose cross-encoder reranking without a legal-domain fine-tuned reranker; the host result fails before device cost is even relevant.

question: Is there a better semantic/BM25 weight than 0.7/0.3 for recall?
lesson: Pure single-metric optimization with no tradeoff; the measured optimum was ~0.9 and recall gains were marginal/invariant for the hard cases (exclusivity ~11% regardless of weight — the bottleneck is chunking/question formulation, not weighting). Do NOT re-propose weight sweeps as a standalone PoC.

question: Does clause-aware chunking (vs fixed page chunks) raise recall@3, especially on hard categories?
lesson: Inconclusive leaning reject: +2.5 overall (below +3 bar, CIs overlap), did NOT move hard categories, and reduced span-integrity. The small gain is not from the registered mechanism. Chunking alone does not fix hard categories.

topic: query formulation (keyword expansion vs decomposition vs gloss)
question: Does reformulating the query (keyword expansion / decomposition / gloss) raise recall@3 and convert to better answers?
lesson: Keyword expansion wins and converts end-to-end: Arm A +4.8 overall recall / Exclusivity 7%->32%; Arm B +3.2 key-fact (Agreement Date +10.7). Gloss hurts. Caveat: Exclusivity isn't key-fact-scorable so its answer-side benefit is unproven. Query reformulation is a real lever.

question: Do cross-reference resolution and static template decomposition raise hard-category recall@3?
lesson: Xref resolution slightly hurt (-0.7) -> reject. Template DECOMPOSITION is a partial win: overall +1.4 and Exclusivity 7%->24% (+17), the FIRST mechanism to move a hard category, but hard-mean +6 fell short of the +10 bar. Decomposition is the most promising hard-category lever.

topic: span-level answer quality on hard categories
question: Does better retrieval (keyword expansion) convert to better hard-category ANSWER quality (span-F1)?
lesson: Gap remains: Exclusivity recall win (+25) converts to only +3.1 span-F1 off a tiny base; hard-mean flat (-0.2), Change-of-Control answers regress. Better retrieval alone does NOT fix hard-category answer quality -- the Qwen2.5-1.5B generator is the bottleneck. Hard-mean span-F1 ~16.1 baseline.

question: Does replacing the Qwen generator with extractive sentence/passage selection improve hard-category answer quality?
lesson: Adopt (host, <=3-sentence passage): hard-mean span-F1 15.7->20.7 (+5.0 vs same-retrieval Qwen), Exclusivity 3.7->12.2. Removing the ~1GB generator HELPS answerable answer quality. Single-sentence under-recalls long clauses; passage window is load-bearing. Confirms Qwen is the answer-step bottleneck (PoC-017).

question: Does a verbatim-extraction prompt + substring validator convert decomposed-retrieval gains into hard-category answer quality?
lesson: Adopt (host) but caveated: hard-mean span-F1 15.4->22.1 (+6.6), Exclusivity +11.8 -- BUT validator reject rate 61.7%, so the first-sentence FALLBACK (not Qwen's constrained generation) carries most of the gain. Effectively retrieval-anchored extraction; overlaps PoC-018. Prefer the cheaper generator-free PoC-018.

question: Does the 'You are a legal expert' authority framing cause Qwen over-refusal, degrading key-fact accuracy?
lesson: Reject, premise inverted: removing authority framing does NOT help (plain +0.9, task-only -0.4 key-fact); the authority prompt has the LOWEST refusal rate. The paper's over-refusal effect does not transfer to Qwen2.5-1.5B on CUAD. Do not re-propose system-prompt framing tweaks for accuracy.

topic: retrieval-confidence (cosine) abstention gate for absent clauses (OP-4)
question: Can a top-1 cosine threshold abstain on absent clauses to cut false-surfacing without hurting recall?
lesson: Reject the global cosine gate: no threshold cuts false-positive >=30% without >3pt recall loss (raw top-1 cosine can't separate absent from answerable; both ~0.6). BUT H1 confirmed OP-4 is real: 75% of absent clauses get a >0.5-cosine match. A single global cosine cut is not a viable abstainer.

question: Does replacing EmbeddingGemma with UIBK-Embedding-v1 MaxSim improve recall@3 within the RAM budget?
lesson: Inconclusive: overall recall@3 61.4->63.2 (+1.8, below +3 bar). Non-Compete +16 (late-interaction helps phrase matching) but Exclusivity -3 -- a redistribution, not a net lift. Do not swap the whole embedder; a smaller/stronger embedder reshuffles rather than lifts hard categories. Device RAM/export unmeasured.

question: Does a per-hard-category semantic/BM25 weight (vs global 0.9) lift hard-category recall@3?
lesson: Reject: calibrated alpha* = 0.9 for ALL hard categories (= global); Delta 0.0. BM25-heavy weighting STRICTLY hurts (0% recall at alpha<=0.5 for Exclusivity/Non-Compete). Hard categories are retrieval-scoring-invariant per-category too, not just globally (extends PoC-013). Do not re-propose hybrid-weight tuning.

topic: 4-bit PTQ of EmbeddingGemma to free RAM (OP-3)
question: Does 4-bit PTQ of EmbeddingGemma preserve recall@3 while freeing >=200MB vs the fp16 600MB baseline?
lesson: Reject as MOOT: we ALREADY ship 4-bit QAT EmbeddingGemma (ggml-org qat-q4_0, ~270MB) -- that IS --embd-gemma-default and produced every committed vector. The 'EmbeddingGemma=600MB fp16' premise is false; H3 RAM target already met. No fp16 baseline exists to quantize. Correct the 600MB framing to ~270MB.

question: Are hard-category gold chunks retrieved-but-truncated (rank 4-10) or not retrieved at all?
lesson: Diagnostic (H1 confirmed, 18.3% gold at rank 4-10). Splits OP-1: Non-Compete is a RANKING problem (25% top-3, 26% at rank 4-10, recall@10 51%) -> a reranker could help; Exclusivity is a REPRESENTATION problem (54% of gold at rank 21+, recall@10 25%) -> depth/reranking can't reach it. The 'filter top-10 then take top-3' intervention is a no-op.

topic: cosine-gated abstention vs Qwen on absent clauses (OP-4)
question: Does a cosine abstention gate beat Qwen generation at correctly declining absent clauses (CAR)?
lesson: Reject, premise inverted: Qwen CAR = 86.3% vs cosine-gate 13.7% (Delta -72.5pp). Qwen reads the text and correctly says 'not stated'; the cosine score can't separate absent from present. Reconciles PoC-021 (the 75% retrieval false-surfacing is caught downstream by Qwen). KEEP Qwen for absent handling. Tension: 018 removes Qwen for quality, 026 keeps it for abstention -> a generator-free pipeline needs its own (non-cosine) abstainer.

topic: cross-encoder reranking of hybrid top-10, hard-category focus (OP-1)
question: Does an off-the-shelf cross-encoder reranker over the hybrid top-10 raise hard-category recall@3?
lesson: Reject (executes PoC-012 host stage, closing it). MiniLM: overall +1.2 (within CI), Non-Compete 25->15; BGE: overall 61.8->49.3, Non-Compete 25->8. Despite PoC-025 proving Non-Compete gold is recoverable at rank 4-10, general-domain MS-MARCO/BGE rerankers DEMOTE legal clauses. Only a legal-domain fine-tuned reranker could help. With 022/023/027, every retrieval-stage lever has failed on hard categories; durable movers are decomposition (016) + answer step (018).
